system.name: VersaPRM
system.one_liner: A multi-domain process reward model made by fine-tuning a math PRM on synthetic, auto-labelled multi-domain chain-of-thought data.

content.variant_note: two dashed lanes run the same chain (dataset, fine-tune, PRM, test-time compute, accuracy-gain chart); the baseline fails outside math, the proposed lane succeeds in all four domains
content.argues: A PRM trained on math helps test-time reasoning only in math; fine-tuning it on synthetic multi-domain data makes it help in Law, Philosophy and Biology too.
content.subject: The Math-PRM pipeline and the VersaPRM pipeline side by side, each ending in an accuracy-gain bar chart over four domains.

lessons.what_to_learn: Draw the baseline and the proposed method as two dashed lanes with the same chain of stages aligned in columns; let the model icon change colour as it is fine-tuned and keep that colour on its result bars; end each lane with a chart topped by ticks or crosses and a one-sentence callout.
lessons.suits: Papers showing that an existing method works in one domain and a data or training change makes it work in many, with the same evaluation pipeline for both.

evidence: Existing open-source PRMs trained on math datasets achieve strong math performance and can outperform a majority voting baseline
these PRMs fail to generalize to other domains (e.g., Law, Philosophy, and Biology), performing no better than the baseline
We propose a multi-domain PRM, VersaPRM, obtained by further fine-tuning a math PRM on a synthetically generated multi-domain dataset

summary: VersaPRM is a process reward model trained on synthetic multi-domain reasoning data, because math-trained PRMs help test-time reasoning only in math. Figure 1 stacks two dashed lanes with the same left-to-right chain. The top lane, (Current) Math PRM, fine-tunes a base LLM gear on a labelled math CoT dataset into a blue Math PRM, runs a test-time compute algorithm fed by a shared Generator LLM and ends in blue bars: a gain of 4.80% in mathematics but about 0.3% in law, philosophy and biology, marked with one tick and three crosses. The bottom lane, (Ours) VersaPRM, generates and auto-labels CoTs for multi-domain questions, further fine-tunes the Math PRM into an orange VersaPRM and ends in four ticked orange bars between 4.3% and 7.9%. Yellow callouts state each verdict.
summary_zh: VersaPRM 用合成的多领域推理数据训练过程奖励模型。图 1 以两条虚线泳道对比：数学 PRM 只在数学上提升 4.80%，其余领域约 0.3% 并标叉；VersaPRM 在四个领域的橙色柱都有提升并标对勾。
notes: Prior kinds kept (paired-lanes). The chart labels and numbers are not in the text layer (the charts are rasters), so the percentages were read from the picture. Three bitmaps of about 87 by 93 pt are placed in the SVG; two are probably the charts and the third could not be identified. The Generator LLM gear straddles the border between the lanes and serves both.
